governance: Plain-English hints for a first-time or occasional diagram author — architecture concepts, never IR mechanics (no registryId, no enum values, no field names). Distinct from sub-layers.json/colors.json/icons.json: those are governed vocabulary validate.ts checks against; this is descriptive copy, never validated, never referenced by the schema itself. Column ids match diagram-schema.json's own columns.* property names; sub-layer ids reuse sub-layers.json's own governed ids directly rather than inventing a second naming scheme. Adding a new column or sub-layer to the schema should add its matching entry here too.

entries.hint: Whoever or whatever originates a request from outside the system — a person, a device, another service calling in. Not part of the platform itself.
The single entry gateway inbound traffic passes through before reaching Core Platform.
The system being described. Organized into up to four sub-layers below — use only the ones that apply.
Infrastructure-level concerns: request routing, API management, policy enforcement. Not business logic.
The actual business logic — the services doing the work described in the requirement.

Named domain concepts (e.g. "Order") modeled as their own thing, distinct from the services above. Most diagrams skip this — only include it if the requirement calls for modeling data concepts separately.
The durable stores of truth — databases, object storage — that Core Platform reads from and writes to.
The outbound boundary Core Platform calls through to reach anything external.
Things outside this platform's ownership — third-party or otherwise-owned services it calls out to.
